title: In-situ simulation for rapid response teams across four hospitals: a stepped multi-site mixed methods evaluation
subtitle: Real-call outcomes, simulation performance and experience across four hospitals introduced in sequence
statement: Rapid response teams in four hospitals train mainly through lectures and online modules, and case reviews show delays in escalation, poor role clarity and weak handovers. The health authority plans monthly unannounced in-situ simulation with structured debriefing, introduced one hospital at a time. It needs a multi-site evaluation that measures what happens in real calls, explains how teams, ward nurses and families experience the change, and handles the few clusters and the ethics of simulating on working wards.
whoAffected: Deteriorating ward patients and their families, rapid response team members (critical care nurses, respiratory therapists, physicians), ward nurses and simulation faculty.
whatHurts: Delays to the first critical intervention and confused roles at the bedside may worsen outcomes for deteriorating patients; families are left without information.
currentPractice: Annual lecture and online module per hospital; no in-situ simulation; case review after serious events.
whyNow: A grant awarded in July 2026, signed participation from all four hospitals, and case review findings the education programme must answer.
constraints: A grant of 48,000 for 18 months; simulation faculty time is limited to 8 hours a month per hospital; unannounced simulations must never delay real patient care and must stop immediately if a real call occurs on the ward.
patientCenteredGoal: Deteriorating ward patients receive critical interventions sooner from teams who know their roles, and families understand what is happening.
summary: Problem framed as a four-hospital stepped mixed methods evaluation of in-situ simulation.
